summary: US-020: A buyer can see which seats are already taken
description:
**As** a buyer looking at a seated performance, **I want** the map to show me which seats are still free, **so that** I can pick one that I will actually get.

**Priority:** P2  **Depends on:** — (TKT-80/US-017 shipped the seat-claim core; TKT-103/104/105 shipped the seat maps)

**The gap.** Every ingredient of a seat picker exists except the one that makes it a picker. Catalog serves the geometry publicly (`GET /public/seat-maps/{seatMapId}`, hours tier per the ADR-004 TKT-107 amendment) and inventory holds seats atomically (`POST /holds/seats`, `claim_seats.released_at IS NULL` is the liveness predicate — ADR-031). But **nothing tells a buyer which seats are occupied**, and nothing on the public catalog contract says a performance is seated at all: `PublicPerformanceDetail` carries `venue` and `ticket_types` and no `seat_map_id`, even though `performances.seat_map_id` has existed since catalog migration 0010. So the storefront can neither discover that a slot is seated nor render occupancy.

**Scope is the read path only.** This story adds no write, no UI, and no selection rules.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Catalog's `PublicPerformanceDetail` gains an optional `seat_map_id` (the published version the slot is seated against; absent for a GA slot), sourced from `performances.seat_map_id`. A GA performance's payload is byte-identical to today's.
- [ ] Inventory serves a public seat-occupancy read for a seated slot returning the slot id, its `seat_map_id`, and the seat identities that are **not claimable right now**. Liveness uses the same predicate the claim path enforces (`claim_seats.released_at IS NULL`, ADR-031) — **not** claim status, which leaks the `finalizing` window.
- [ ] The read declares and emits ADR-004 rule 1's **seconds** tier (`public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`), the same tier as `getAvailability`, declared in the contract as a single-value enum so ADR-028's response validator fails closed on drift — the shape TKT-110 established for `AvailabilityCacheControl`.
- [ ] A GA slot is refused with a 409 (it has no seats), and an unknown slot with a 404 — distinguishable, not collapsed.
- [ ] The occupancy query is scoped by pool and proven scoped: a test asserts both the result set and that the plan uses `claim_seats_one_live_per_seat` / `claim_seats_by_claim` rather than a sequential scan (ADR-019's two-test rule, applied to inventory).
- [ ] Both specs declared, generated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) committed before the gate, and the new operations covered by the smoke suite (ADR-009 / ADR-028 / ADR-030).

Quality gates: `make check` green; contract tests; `organizer_id`-scoped where the surrounding operations are. **This ticket moves no money and issues no ticket.**

objective.note: Without it a seat picker cannot exist: the buyer has geometry but no occupancy, and cannot even tell a seated performance from a GA one.

scope.note: IN: the catalog `seat_map_id` exposure, the inventory occupancy read, its cache tier, its error taxonomy, its index proof. OUT: any UI (TKT-174), any write (TKT-173), orphan rules (TKT-175), best-available (TKT-81).

uncertainties.note: Whether the occupancy read lives at `/slots/{id}/seats` or extends `/slots/{id}/availability` with a seat list is a Planning-time call. A separate path is the more reversible option (it does not change an existing hot response shape) and is the presumed default; the AC constrains the observable properties, not the URL.

dependencies.note: None open. TKT-80 (seat claims), TKT-103/104/105 (seat maps, publish, edit), TKT-110 (the declared-tier pattern) are all merged.

approach.note: Mirror `getAvailability` end to end — the handler, the declared single-value cache header, the 404/409 taxonomy and the smoke registration all have a working precedent one operation away in the same service.

first_slice.note: One seated slot with one held seat: the read returns exactly that identity, at the seconds tier.

success.note: Demoable through the gateway with curl: hold a seat, watch it appear in the occupancy read, release it, watch it leave.

context_memo.note: Baked at decomposition (2026-08-01). Re-resolve `governingAdrs` against docs/adr/ at claim time — ADR-029/031 are recent and this epic's area is actively moving.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate — keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and capability map (US-017/US-018 are the seat-claim core; this epic is the buyer-facing picker)

governingAdrs.why: Fixes the tier: remaining availability is the **seconds** tier (`max-age=5`), and seat-map geometry is the hours tier. Occupancy is availability, not geometry — do not inherit the seat-map tier just because the payload names seats. Rule 1 also requires the tier be *declared*, not merely emitted.

The response validator fails closed, so a declared header the handler does not emit (or vice versa) is a 5xx, not a lint warning. The single-value enum + handler constant pairing (`CacheControlPublicAvailability`) is the shape that survives it.

`released_at IS NULL` — not claim status — is the liveness predicate for a seat. Reading occupancy by status leaks the `finalizing` window and shows a sold seat as free. Also: expired holds are swept lazily on the next seat hold, so a quiet pool can carry stale live rows; decide deliberately whether the read sweeps, filters on `expires_at`, or reports them.

Written for catalog but its rule is general and this AC applies it here: a scoped read is only scoped if an index backs the filter, and proving it takes two tests (the result is scoped **and** the scan is).
Contract-first: both specs change, both generated artifacts are committed **before** the gate runs, or `check-generate` reads the regen as drift.
Defines what the coverage gate demands of a new catalog operation — the `seat_map_id` field lands on an existing operation, so check whether that trips the gate's scope.

The claim transaction owns the lock order and the pool row. A read that takes locks in a different order, or holds one across an HTTP call, is the classic way to deadlock the on-sale path this read is meant to serve.

### Claimed — TKT-172

**Selection reason.** Only claimable child of TKT-35: zero open blockers (`links: []`), and it blocks the other three (172 → 173 → 174 → 175), so it has maximum unblocking power in this epic. Nothing else is in flight.

**Blocker check.** Zero `blocked-by` edges. Its own dependencies — TKT-80 (seat claims), TKT-103/104/105 (seat maps), TKT-110 (the declared-cache-tier pattern) — are all merged to `main`.

**Branch.** `TKT-172-seat-occupancy-read`, cut from `origin/main` at `1883a4e5`.

---

### ⚠️ Gate waiver — this ticket runs GATELESS

The repo owner has **deliberately waived all four human gates** for TKT-35 and its children, as a process experiment, and instructed the agent to run Ready → Done in one continuous pass. Recording it here so the board history shows which tickets ran without human gates.

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority | human drags Backlog → Ready | given by the owner's instruction at decomposition |
| 2 — plan approval | human drags Planning → Building | agent resolves open decisions itself: prefer what the cross-model critique recommends; absent a recommendation, pick the most reversible option. Every self-made decision and its rationale is recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 — review + merge | human reviews the PR and squash-merges | agent squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges (same triage, second-pass and churn-cap rules). The review-guide is still posted on the PR first — it becomes the audit record. |
| 4 — PO acceptance | PO validates and drags to Done | agent self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code, posts the validation note, closes with the full metrics comment. |

**Unchanged and non-negotiable:** `config.models` routing (no substitutions), cross-model review for both plan and code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check` green before every push and after the merge, every marker comment posted, no AI attribution in commits or PRs.

**Standing stop conditions** (the agent halts and reports instead of proceeding): the gate or CI fails twice on the same cause with no clear fix; the work would touch auth, money paths, data migrations or CI/deploy config in a way the ticket and plan did not anticipate; a blocking review finding survives the churn cap; a configured model is unreachable after the documented escalation ladder; or a destructive/irreversible action's right choice is ambiguous.

**Stop-condition pre-check for this ticket:** it adds a read endpoint and one optional response field. It moves no money, issues no ticket, and touches no auth or CI config. It *does* need an inventory migration only if the occupancy query needs an index that `0009_seat_claims.sql` does not already provide — `claim_seats_one_live_per_seat (pool_id, seat_identity) WHERE released_at IS NULL` and `claim_seats_by_claim (claim_id)` both exist, so the expectation is **no migration**. If Planning concludes otherwise, that is a data-migration touch the ticket did not anticipate and the run stops here for a human.

### Execution plan — TKT-172 (draft)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex, effort high, read-only — no `--write`), per `config.models.plan`. Run: `task --prompt-file .plan-brief.172.md --model gpt-5.6-sol --effort high --background`, job `task-msb17xe4-3q490m`, completed, conclusive.

The brief it was given carried the ticket, the six ACs, the eight governing ADRs with what each constrains *for this ticket*, the verbatim binding gate rule from `AGENTS.md`, and pointers into the real code (the `getAvailability` precedent, the `claim_seats` schema, the `liveClaims`/`consumingClaims` predicates, the lazy `sweepExpired` path, the catalog public select, and the smoke-coverage machinery). The drafter read the code itself; nothing below is taken on trust — every seam it names was re-verified at HEAD before this was posted (see the plan-review comment).

---

## 1. Definition of Done

- [ ] **AC1:** `PublicPerformanceDetail` declares optional UUID `seat_map_id`; `publicPerformancesSelect` hydrates it from `performances.seat_map_id`; event and season detail emit it for seated slots. Ordinary GA and festival-day objects omit the key and retain their current serialized bytes.
- [ ] **AC2:** `GET /slots/{id}/seat-occupancy?organizer_id={uuid}` returns `slot_id`, inventory’s bound `seat_map_id`, and sorted `unavailable_seat_identities`. Held/unexpired, `finalizing`, and confirmed claims are included; released, expired, and due-but-unswept held claims are excluded.
- [ ] **AC3:** The occupancy `200` declares a required single-value `Cache-Control` enum and emits exactly `public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`; missing or different values fail closed under ADR-028.
- [ ] **AC4:** An organizer-scoped pool miss returns 404. An existing GA pool returns 409 through the existing `ErrPoolKindMismatch` branch in `problem()`.
- [ ] **AC5:** The result test proves another pool cannot leak seats into the response. A separate EXPLAIN smoke test proves the shipped query reaches `claim_seats` through `claim_seats_one_live_per_seat` and performs no sequential scan of that relation.
- [ ] **AC6:** Both OpenAPI specs are updated; generated Go and catalog-derived TypeScript artifacts are committed before the gate; the real-stack smoke suite drives the catalog field and the new inventory operation through the gateway; `make check` passes.

## 2. The test seam

The first red test goes in a **new** real-Postgres file, `services/inventory/internal/store/seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go`:

- `TestSeatOccupancyResultIsPoolScopedAndUsesClaimLiveness`
- `TestSeatOccupancyDistinguishesUnknownAndGA`
- `TestSeatOccupancyIsIndexScoped`

This is the first seam because the risky behavior is relational: partial-index liveness, lazy expiry, cross-pool scoping, confirmed/finalizing handling, and PostgreSQL’s actual plan. A plain `*_test.go` with mocks cannot establish any of those. Initially the test will fail to compile because the proposed `(*Postgres).SeatOccupancy` method is absent; after a minimal stub it must remain red on the expected result set before SQL is implemented.

Additional tests, still written before their corresponding implementation:

- **Existing** `services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_publish_smoke_test.go`: add `TestPublishedEventReadCarriesSeatMapID` so the positional `publicPerformancesSelect`/`rows.Scan` path is exercised against PostgreSQL.
- **Existing** `services/catalog/internal/api/seatmap_test.go`: add `TestPublicPerformanceDetailSeatMapID` through `env.do`, covering the generated response type and real contract validator.
- **Existing** `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go`: extend `TestPublicDetail` and `TestFestivalPublicGroupedRead` with GA/festival omission assertions.
- **Existing** `services/inventory/internal/api/availability_cache_tier_test.go`: add `TestSeatOccupancyCacheTierIsContractEnforced`, modeled on `TestAvailabilityCacheTierIsContractEnforced`.
- **Existing** `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go`: extend `TestSeatedPublicationCoexistsWithGA` to drive both public reads through the gateway.

## 3. Files to change

Hand-written:

- `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` — add optional UUID `seat_map_id` to `PublicPerformanceDetail`; do not add it to `required`.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go` — add `p.seat_map_id` to `publicPerformancesSelect`, scan through `uuid.NullUUID`, and populate the existing `Performance.SeatMapID`.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go` — copy `pa.Performance.SeatMapID` into generated `PublicPerformanceDetail.SeatMapId` in `publicEventDetail`; leave the festival-day builder nil.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/seatmap_test.go` — add the seated public-detail contract test.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go` — pin ordinary GA and festival-day omission, including the GA raw-object regression.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_publish_smoke_test.go` — test real-Postgres public hydration for seated and GA performances.
- `services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml` — declare `getSeatOccupancy`, its response schema, 400/404/409/500 responses, and its required seconds-tier header.
- `services/inventory/internal/store/seat_claims.go` — add the proposed `SeatOccupancy` result type, production `seatOccupancyQuery` constant, and `(*Postgres).SeatOccupancy`.
- `services/inventory/internal/store/seat_occupancy_smoke_test.go` — **new file** for liveness, error distinction, result scoping, and EXPLAIN proof.
- `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go` — mount the public GET, parse the existing path/query identifiers, call the store, emit the cache header, and use `problem()` for errors.
- `services/inventory/internal/api/availability_cache_tier_test.go` — pin the new header constant/declaration pair, including missing and wrong values.
- `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go` — assert catalog discovery, empty/occupied inventory responses, cache header, GA 409, unknown 404, and thereby register `getSeatOccupancy` with smoke coverage.

Generated by `make generate`:

- `services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`
- `web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts`
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts`

Intentional non-changes:

- No migration file.
- No `gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go`: `/api/inventory/` already proxies every non-`internal` child path.
- No `smoke/coverage_test.go`: `getWithHeaders` calls `validateServiceResponse`, which automatically records `getSeatOccupancy`; the unfiltered coverage gate then enforces it.
- No storefront or back-office implementation beyond regenerated catalog types.
- No catalog festival SQL change: `publishedFestivalPerformancesQuery` reads only grouped festival days, which `CreatePerformance` forbids from being seated.

## 4. Design decisions

- **Endpoint and shape:** choose `GET /slots/{id}/seat-occupancy?organizer_id=…`, operation ID `getSeatOccupancy`, returning:

  ```json
  {
    "slot_id": "uuid",
    "seat_map_id": "uuid",
    "unavailable_seat_identities": ["Orchestra/A/1"]
  }
  ```

  The list is sorted by `seat_identity` and is `[]`, not `null`, when empty. Reject embedding geometry: catalog already owns it, and joining service databases violates ADR-002. Reject buyer/session-specific data: this is a shared-cacheable public read.

- **Liveness:** query `claim_seats` with both `cs.released_at IS NULL` and the existing `consumingClaims` predicate from `channel_allocations.go`. This includes confirmed plus `liveClaims`—held/unexpired and `finalizing`.

  Reject raw claim status because it can omit `finalizing`. Reject `liveClaims` alone because it omits confirmed sales. Reject `released_at IS NULL` alone because it reports lazily-unswept expired holds as occupied.

- **Expired holds:** filter a due held claim out using `expires_at > now()` via `consumingClaims`, but do not sweep it. The next claim transaction would sweep and release it before attempting the unique-index insert, so it is claimable in fact. A cacheable GET must remain non-writing and lock-free; sweeping would turn it into a mutation and introduce pool-lock contention.

- **Query shape:** use one organizer-scoped SELECT rooted at `inventory_pools`, left-joining the live seat rows. This distinguishes an empty seated pool from an unknown pool without a cross-service call. It takes no row or advisory locks and holds nothing across HTTP.

- **GA versus unknown:** zero pool rows yields existing `ErrNotFound` → 404. A returned pool with `inventory_kind != 'seated'` or no valid `seat_map_id` yields existing `ErrPoolKindMismatch` → 409 through the already-shipped `problem()` branch. No new error type is needed.

- **Which `seat_map_id` inventory echoes:** use `inventory_pools.seat_map_id`, provisioned from catalog’s schema-4 publication. Reject calling catalog at read time: it adds failure/latency to the hot read and violates service ownership. Catalog independently emits `performances.seat_map_id`; consumers can detect eventual projection skew without either service joining the other.

- **Catalog publication semantics:** expose the field only on performances already returned by `p.status='published'`. `CreatePerformance` verifies the referenced map is published at binding time; migration `0010_publish_seat_maps.sql`’s composite FK guarantees only map existence plus matching organizer and venue. Do not rejoin or filter on current seat-map status: the field names the exact version the performance was bound to, not the family’s newest version.

- **Cache declaration:** add a dedicated `SeatOccupancyCacheControl` header component and `CacheControlPublicSeatOccupancy` constant with the same seconds-tier value. Reusing the existing names was rejected because their current comments describe `getAvailability` specifically; the explicit pair keeps each operation’s declaration and emission independently fail-closed.

## 5. Test plan

- Catalog store:

  - Seated and GA performances under one published event.
  - `GetPublishedEvent` returns the exact bound map for the seated performance and nil for GA.
  - This catches a missing `p.seat_map_id` projection or mismatched positional scan.

- Catalog API:

  - Seated public event detail contains the exact UUID.
  - Ordinary GA’s nested performance object matches a pre-change raw JSON literal, proving omission rather than merely decoding into a nil pointer.
  - `TestFestivalPublicGroupedRead` confirms festival days still omit the shared optional field.
  - Draft/archived slots remain absent through the existing published predicate.

- Inventory store:

  - Include unexpired held, `finalizing`, and confirmed seats.
  - Exclude released seats.
  - Backdate a held claim’s `expires_at` while leaving `status='held'` and `released_at IS NULL`; exclude it and then verify the GET did not mutate either column.
  - Exclude claims from another pool, including the same seat identity.
  - Return sorted identities and a non-nil empty slice.
  - Echo the requested slot and pool’s seat map.
  - Unknown/wrong-organizer pool → `ErrNotFound`; GA pool → `ErrPoolKindMismatch`.

- Index proof:

  - EXPLAIN the proposed `seatOccupancyQuery` constant—the exact production statement, not a reduced copy.
  - Mirror catalog’s `explainGenericPlan`: server-side `PREPARE`, `SET LOCAL plan_cache_mode=force_generic_plan`, `EXPLAIN EXECUTE`, and assert both `$1` and `$2` survive.
  - Seed enough foreign pools/claims to make a sequential scan unattractive, run `ANALYZE`, assert `claim_seats_one_live_per_seat` appears, and reject `Seq Scan on claim_seats`.

- Cache contract:

  - `CacheControlPublicSeatOccupancy` validates as 200.
  - A missing header and a different tier each become 500.
  - Real-stack smoke confirms the actual handler emits the exact header.

- HTTP/smoke:

  - Before a hold: seated response is empty with correct IDs/header.
  - After `postSeatHold`: response contains `Orchestra/A/1`.
  - GA slot returns 409; random slot returns 404.
  - Catalog detail identifies the seated performance and leaves the GA performance unchanged.
  - The validated 200 records `inventory getSeatOccupancy`; no allowlist entry is permitted.

- Execution order:

  - Run the targeted tests red before store/handler implementation.
  - Implement and run targeted plain and `-tags smoke` suites green.
  - Run `make generate`, review all four generated paths, and commit regenerated artifacts before invoking the gate.
  - On a clean clone run `make deps`; finish with `make check`.

## 6. Risks

1. **Incorrect liveness around expiry or checkout.** Raw status loses `finalizing`; raw child-row liveness retains expired holds; `liveClaims` loses confirmed seats. The lifecycle matrix and due-unswept non-mutation test catch each variant.
2. **Catalog positional scan drift.** Adding the SELECT column without the matching `rows.Scan` target fails only at runtime. The catalog store smoke test and real-stack public-detail request catch it.
3. **A logically scoped query still scans all seats.** The existing index makes a migration unnecessary, but only the EXPLAIN test establishes that the shipped SQL actually uses it under seeded statistics.
4. **Contract/header drift becomes a production 500.** This is intentional ADR-028 behavior; the focused cache-tier test catches missing, mismatched, or weakened enum declarations before smoke.
5. **Projection lag between catalog and inventory.** Catalog can expose seating before the publication consumer has provisioned inventory, temporarily yielding inventory 404. This already exists for availability; smoke must retry provisioning before asserting occupancy. The ticket should not add a synchronous catalog call.
6. **Optional field accidentally changes GA bytes.** Generated `*UUID` plus `omitempty`, the raw GA golden, and festival regression catch this.
7. **Planner-test brittleness.** Seeded statistics and a future PostgreSQL version may choose a different valid plan. Keep the assertion narrow: index presence plus no sequential scan on `claim_seats`, not every join node.

**Migration status: no migration is needed.** `claim_seats_one_live_per_seat (pool_id, seat_identity) WHERE released_at IS NULL` exactly backs the scoped live-child predicate, while claims are reached by their existing key. If the production query cannot be made to use that index in the required EXPLAIN proof, stop and escalate rather than adding an index silently.

## 7. Open decisions

None remain unresolved from HEAD. The endpoint name, response vocabulary, non-writing expiry treatment, inventory-side map echo, and catalog publication behavior are fixed above. The only stop condition is the unexpected failure of the existing partial index to support the exact production query under the required plan proof.
